narration.full_text: Let's delve into the fascinating world of plant movements, specifically focusing on geotropism. Geotropic movement is how plant parts respond to gravity. The phenomenon itself is called geotropism. When the stem tip grows upwards, away from Earth's gravitational pull, it's known as negative geotropism. Think of it as defying gravity! Conversely, when root tips grow downwards, towards gravity, it's called positive geotropism. This ensures roots anchor the plant and absorb water and nutrients from the soil. So, to summarize, stems typically exhibit negative geotropism, growing upwards towards the light, while roots show positive geotropism, growing downwards into the soil.

items: Geotropic movement: Plant part movement in response to gravity.
Negative Geotropism: Stem tip grows away from Earth's gravitational forces.
Positive Geotropism: Root tips grow towards gravity.
